inputs.original_text: John Lahart is right that people without children should not be treated as less deserving of fairness. But that cannot become a pretext to weaken the right of families to pass on what they have worked to build. Inheritance is more than privilege: it is a way parents and relatives support the next generation and preserve a family’s security. A fair system should respect different family circumstances without turning every family legacy into an excuse for greater state control or redistribution.
inputs.modified_text: John Lahart is right that people without children deserve fairness. But fairness should not mean treating family inheritance as something the state is entitled to weaken or redistribute. Families should be free to pass on what they have built, providing security for the next generation and preserving the bonds of responsibility across generations. Respecting people’s different circumstances must not become an excuse for greater state control.
